short: Explicit tone stage (M06) is new among Mandarin lip readers but standard: one run, one split, a 1.59-point CER margin; hosts overlap train and test, and CER is 50.08% on unseen hosts.
position: CSSMCM [@zhao2019cascade] adds an explicit tone stage between pinyin syllables and characters (M06) and builds CMLR with ASR-generated references (M11). The tone stage has no prior in Mandarin lip-reading decoders [@zhang2019lipchnet; @zhou2019modality], but its support is one 1.59-point CER margin over a re-implemented LipCH-Net from one run on one random split, so it is standard rather than ahead. All 11 hosts appear in both training and test under the dataset authors' split, and CSSMCM rises from 32.48% to 50.08% CER on unseen hosts [@xue2023lipformer]. CMLR's labels are unchecked ASR output, unlike the checked manuscripts of LipCH-Net. The same group's [concurrent] LIBS reaches 31.27% without tones [@zhao2020hearing], and today's best CMLR figure, 7.89%, uses toneless pinyin with LLM refinement [@sun2025vallrpin].
